title: Comparison of the framework and PBC rational coefficient systems
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, and an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $T$ be a noetherian finite-dimensional scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible, as in [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization]. For each finite field $E/\Ql$ in $\Qlb$, denote by $\mathcal C^{\mathrm{sf}}_E(T)$ the raw rationalization [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] and by $\mathcal C^{\mathrm{pbc}}_E(T)$ the raw rationalization [def-weil-pbc-rational-category]. Write $T^{\mathrm{sf}}_{L/E}$ and $T^{\mathrm{pbc}}_{L/E}$ for their scalar-extension functors, respectively those of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] and [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension].

There are canonical exact $E$-linear equivalences
$$J_{T,E}:\mathcal C^{\mathrm{sf}}_E(T)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal C^{\mathrm{pbc}}_E(T)$$
induced by the identity on the common full integral category of [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization]: $J_{T,E}(K)=K$ on integral objects and $J_{T,E}(u\otimes e)=u\otimes e$ on localized Hom groups. For $E\subset L$, the natural isomorphisms
$$j_{T,L/E}:J_{T,L}T^{\mathrm{sf}}_{L/E}\xrightarrow{\sim}T^{\mathrm{pbc}}_{L/E}J_{T,E}$$
are the rationalizations of the inverses of the specified completion maps $\chi_{L/E}$ of [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]. They respect identities, shifts, and the specified scalar associators [lem-weil-scalar-extension-composition, prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension], including the unit and three-field cocycle equations.

These equivalences induce an exact $\Qlb$-linear equivalence
$$J_T:\mathcal C_T\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal P_T$$
from [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] to [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category]. It sends $(E,K)$ to $(E,J_{T,E}K)$, and a common-stage arrow to its $J_{T,L}$-image conjugated by the source and target maps $j_{T,L/E}$. It identifies the Hom colimits, finite-stage inclusions, shifts and common-stage distinguished triangles, with no Karoubi completion.

For any scheme isomorphism $h:U\xrightarrow{\sim}T$ between schemes satisfying the same hypotheses, these equivalences commute with the rational and common-stage pullbacks induced respectively by [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. The comparison is the identity on the common finite-reduction pullback tower, with the composition and scalar comparisons normalized by [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization]. It is compatible with identity and composition of scheme isomorphisms and with the maps $j_{T,L/E}$. In particular for a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme $X_0$ [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ and $g_X=\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$, geometric Frobenius [def-weil-frobenius-detailed], one has $J_X Lg_X^{*,\mathrm{sf}}\cong Lg_X^{*,\mathrm{pbc}}J_X$ compatibly with all finite stages. Consequently the equivalence identifies the categories of Weil pairs of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex] with the pairs for that PBC pullback, including their intertwining morphisms.

proof.text: For each finite $E$, apply the integral characterization to $T$: its noetherian, finite-dimensional and invertibility hypotheses are exactly those assumed here. Both integral categories are the same full subcategory of $D(\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,T})$, with the same reduction functors, not merely categories with equivalent lists of objects. The identity therefore gives mutually inverse $\mathcal O_E$-linear functors on objects and all ambient derived morphisms. Shifts and distinguished triangles are inherited from that ambient derived category; the characterization's closure under shifts and cones makes this identification exact in both directions.

source.place: Proposition 6.6.11 and Proposition 6.8.11(3); applied through the stated integral characterization

proof.text: Use the raw Hom descriptions in the two rationalization definitions. Set $J_{T,E}K=K$ and $J_{T,E}(u\otimes e)=u\otimes e$. The balancing relation $(au)\otimes e=u\otimes ae$ is the same on both sides. Composition is $(v\otimes b)(u\otimes e)=(vu)\otimes be$, so this assignment preserves composition and identities and is $E$-linear. Its inverse has exactly the same formulas. Both shifts come from the common integral shift. By the scalar-localization triangulation theorem, both sets of distinguished triangles consist of triangles isomorphic to images of the same integral distinguished triangles. Thus $J_{T,E}$ and its inverse are exact; no retract is added.

source.place: Final sentence; explicit comparison of the two coefficient conventions

proof.text: Put $R_F=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,T}$. Framework scalar extension is the strict quotient-tower completion of $K\otimes^L_{R_E}R_L$, whereas PBC scalar extension is ordinary completed-ring change of coefficients. The common integral objects are derived complete by step 1, so the specified map $\chi_{L/E,K}$ is invertible. Define $j_{T,L/E,K}$ as its inverse, followed by rationalization. Naturality of $\chi$ gives naturality on every integral derived arrow. Tensoring the naturality equation with $e\in E$ and adding proves it for every rational arrow. The quotient-map definition of $\chi$ commutes with shifts: shifting the quotient complexes and the product-cone map shifts both its quotient component and its zero component. Hence $j$ respects the exact-functor shift comparisons. For $L=E$, $\chi$ is the completeness unit, so its inverse followed by the multiplication identification gives precisely the normalized identity transition.

source.place: Final sentence; explicit comparison of the two coefficient conventions

proof.text:
Write $S_{L/E}$ and $P_{L/E}$ for the framework and PBC transitions. The specified framework associator is the ordinary tensor associator conjugated by the completion maps $\chi$; this normalization is explicitly part of the pullback-realization lemma, while PBC uses tensor balancing. Consequently, for $E\subset L\subset M$, their components obey
$$a^p_{M,L,E}\,P_{M/L}(j_{L/E})\,j_{M/L,S_{L/E}K}=j_{M/E}\,J_{T,M}(a^s_{M,L,E}).$$
Indeed substitute $j=\chi^{-1}$ and the conjugated formula for $a^s$: every adjacent $\chi\chi^{-1}$ cancels, using naturality to move a coefficient-change arrow across $\chi$. The remaining map on an ordinary tensor representative is $((x\otimes b)\otimes c)\mapsto x\otimes bc$ on either side. The two unit cases give $x\otimes1\mapsto x$; for four fields both composites give $(((x\otimes b)\otimes c)\otimes d)\mapsto x\otimes bcd$. This proves the unit, three-field cocycle and further associativity equations for the specified maps, and rationalization preserves these equations.

source.place: Final sentence; explicit comparison of the two coefficient conventions

proof.text:
For objects $(E,K),(F,H)$ and a common field $L$, send $u:S_{L/E}K\to S_{L/F}H$ to
$$\Phi_L(u)=j_{L/F,H}\,J_{T,L}(u)\,j_{L/E,K}^{-1}.$$
This is a bijection of Hom groups, with inverse obtained by applying $J_{T,L}^{-1}$ to $j_{L/F,H}^{-1}v j_{L/E,K}$. For $L\subset M$, transition in either pair category is $u\mapsto a_{M,L,F}\,T_{M/L}(u)\,a_{M,L,E}^{-1}$. Substitution of the equation in step 4 at the source and target, followed by naturality of $j_{M/L}$, gives $\Phi_M(u_M)=(\Phi_Lu)_M$. Thus $\Phi$ and its inverse preserve eventual equality of representatives and define inverse maps on the displayed Hom colimits. They preserve sums. At one common stage the middle factors $j^{-1}j$ cancel in $\Phi(v)\Phi(u)$, giving $\Phi(vu)$, and $\Phi(1)=1$. This defines $J_T$ on arrows and proves it fully faithful.

source.place: Final sentence; explicit comparison of the two coefficient conventions

proof.text: Every PBC pair $(E,H)$ is the image of $(E,J_{T,E}^{-1}H)$, so $J_T$ is an equivalence. It commutes with finite-stage inclusions by the unit case of step 4. If $\alpha\in\Qlb$, choose a common finite stage containing $\alpha$ and the arrow's stage. The map $\Phi$ is linear over that field, so $\Phi(\alpha u)=\alpha\Phi(u)$; hence $J_T$ is $\Qlb$-linear. The shift compatibility of $j$ identifies the shifted common-stage arrow formulas. A common-stage distinguished triangle is sent, by the conjugating isomorphisms $j$ at its vertices, to the image of its $J_{T,L}$-triangle. Step 2 makes that triangle distinguished. The inverse has the same property. The definition of distinguished triangles therefore makes $J_T$ exact in both directions, with the prescribed shifts and common-stage cones. All constructions used only the objects $(E,K)$ already present.

source.place: Final sentence; explicit comparison of the two coefficient conventions

proof.text:
For a scheme isomorphism $h:U\to T$ choose one flat-term K-flat representative $P$ of a common integral object $K$. In both definitions of completed pullback the strict tower is
$$Q_n=\operatorname{Res}_n h_n^*(P\otimes_{R_E}(A_{E,n})_T),$$
with the actual quotient transition maps. The framework realizes this tower by its product cone, while PBC realizes it by derived inverse limit. Use the realization identification in the integral comparison lemma to identify these models. More explicitly, for a K-injective tower replacement $Q\to I$, the Roos comparison is $\lim I\to\operatorname{Cone}(1-s_I)[-1]$, $z\mapsto(0,z)$. Exact countable products make the cone map from $Q$ to $I$ a quasi-isomorphism. Their zigzag identifies the two realizations of the identity map of the entire tower, naturally for tower arrows; it does not infer equality from equality of individual reductions. The K-injective existence theorem applies to the small ringed tower site, and supplies enough injectives also on the underlying site. The integral well-definedness theorem identifies this construction independently of the K-flat representative, so the natural tower comparison descends to derived morphisms. This constructs an integral comparison $b_{h,E}:J_{U,E}F^s_{h,E}\to F^p_{h,E}J_{T,E}$. The framework preservation theorem and step 1 show both objects lie in the common integral constructible subcategory, so the comparison restricts there.

source.place: Final sentence; explicit comparison of the two coefficient conventions

proof.text: For identity and composable scheme isomorphisms use the simultaneous quotient diagrams and their tower counits specified in the integral realization lemma. On the common finite tower the comparison $b$ is the identity. Thus the two routes around the composition square apply the same termwise module-pullback composition map and the same counit of the whole strict tower. Realizing this equality gives the composition equation for $b$; the identity case uses the identity tower map. For coefficient extension $E\subset L$, the same lemma specifies both iterated identifications by the tower counit, coefficient quotient actions and tensor associators. The map $\chi$ used in step 3 is its specified quotient-map completion unit (zero shifted-product component). PBC uses ordinary tensor balancing and the same quotient actions. Inserting $\chi^{-1}$ on the framework scalar side therefore cancels its completion unit, and both resulting diagrams use the same coefficient action and pullback map on each simultaneous quotient complex. This is an equality of whole derived quotient diagrams, including their counits, before realization. The realization lemma's composition/scalar and successive-extension equations, together with the PBC scalar comparison, give the corresponding mixed squares for $b$ and $j$, as well as their unit and shift compatibilities.

source.place: Final sentence; explicit comparison of the two coefficient conventions

proof.text: Rationalize $b_{h,E}$: its integral naturality equation remains true after tensoring by $e\in E$ and adding, exactly as in step 3. For a common-stage arrow $u$, both composites in the naturality square for the induced $b_h:J_UF^s_h\to F^p_hJ_T$ are the class of $F^p_{h,L}(\Phi_Lu)$ with the scalar comparison at the source and its inverse at the target. To see this, substitute the pullback arrow formula from the framework definition and $\Phi_L$ from step 5; apply the mixed square of step 8 to move $b$ past each scalar comparison. The adjacent inverse comparison factors then cancel. Eventual equality is respected by step 5, so this gives a natural isomorphism on the common-stage categories. The identity, composition and scalar equations from step 8 survive rationalization and passage to classes. This proves the asserted compatibility at every finite stage and on $\Qlb$.

source.place: Final sentence; explicit comparison of the two coefficient conventions

proof.text: For the final specialization $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, a finite affine finite-type cover of $X_0$ base changes to a finite affine cover whose algebras are finite type over $k$: the images of the original generators still generate after tensoring with $k$. Thus $X$ is finite type over the field $k$. A field has only the ideals $0$ and the unit ideal, so $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian; the finite-type-over-Noetherian lemma makes $X$ Noetherian, and the finite-type dimension lemma gives finite dimension. The image of the nonzero element $\ell$ of $k$ is a unit in every local ring, since $\ell\ne p$. Finally $g_X$ is the scheme automorphism of the Frobenius definition, with the displayed inverse. Apply step 9 to this isomorphism. Nothing requires it to be a $k$-morphism.

source.place: Final sentence; explicit comparison of the two coefficient conventions

proof.text: Write $F_s=Lg_X^{*,s}$, $F_p=Lg_X^{*,p}$ and $b:J_XF_s\to F_pJ_X$ for the comparison. Send a Weil pair $(K,\theta:F_sK\xrightarrow{\sim}K)$ to $(J_XK,J_X(\theta)b_K^{-1})$ and an arrow $u$ to $J_X(u)$. Naturality says $F_p(J_Xu)b_K=b_HJ_X(F_su)$. It follows by multiplication by $b_K^{-1}$ that the intertwining equation $u\theta=\theta'F_su$ is equivalent, by full faithfulness of $J_X$, to the intertwining equation for its image. Hence the pair functor is fully faithful. Given a PBC pair $(J_XK,\psi)$, the unique preimage of $\psi b_K$ under the Hom bijection is an isomorphism $\theta:F_sK\to K$ (lift its inverse as well); its image pair is the given pair. Every PBC underlying object has this form by step 6. Thus the functor is essentially surjective too. The construction at a finite stage uses $b_{g_X,E}$, and step 9 identifies it with the common-stage construction, proving the last compatibility clause.
